title: Hanji Myeongjo — Exhibition Threshold
description: A museum-grade opening folio built on digitised 닥종이 grain, where a single Myeongjo title floats in restrained sumi-ink against warm handmade-paper cream. Distinguished from generic Korean templates by its strict adherence to MMCA and Leeum print-catalogue stillness — one title, one vermillion seal, one breath.
philosophy: This design borrows the visual grammar of Korean museum print culture, where a single folio page can carry one title, one seal mark, and nothing else — and be complete. It refuses decorative pattern, hero photography, and Western symmetrical grid logic, reaching instead for the asymmetric placement found in classical East Asian book layout and contemporary institutional dorok. The vermillion seal is not ornament; it is authorship made physically present. It exists for curators, scholars, and cultural institutions who need a digital surface that honours material culture without merely costuming itself in it.
goodFor: Museum and gallery exhibition opening title slides
Artist statement and print-catalogue introductions on lobby or preview screens
Academic art criticism lectures in Korean, Chinese, or Japanese institutional contexts
Cultural-institution announcements requiring understated typographic gravitas
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews needing dense data grids
High-energy startup pitch decks requiring bold colour contrast and kinetic layout
Children's educational content or playful consumer-brand presentations
Multi-column newsletter or infographic layouts where texture competes with information density
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should evoke the hush of a Korean museum print-catalogue opening folio — materially present, self-sufficient, and entirely still. A single title mark drifts in sumi-ink depth against warm handmade-paper ground, its isolation producing weight rather than emptiness. The only chromatic event is a vermillion seal, small and precisely placed, its intensity reading as authorship and ritual rather than decorative punctuation. Avoid symmetrical centering, photographic heroes, and any layered ornamentation — the grain of the paper is the visual event.

examples.layoutNotes: The slide uses a full-bleed hanji texture as ground with no framing band or border — the paper surface is the canvas. The title block is placed low-left on an asymmetric vertical axis, occupying the lower third of the field so the upper expanse reads as intentional negative space, not vacancy. The vermillion seal mark sits in the lower-right quadrant, acting as a gravitational counterweight to the title rather than a decorative accent. No header band, no footer rule, no page number; the folio declares itself complete through restraint alone.

examples.promptCore: The slide evokes a single folio page from a Leeum or MMCA exhibition catalogue — austere, deliberate, charged with negative space. Body text breathes against the warm hanji ground in a single column leaning centre-right, leaving the generous left margin as meditative emptiness. The only chromatic note is the vermillion seal anchoring the lower corner as authorship, not decoration. Avoid illustrative fill, gradient wash, or symmetrical framing — asymmetry and restraint are the entire composition.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column asymmetric grid; body text occupies cols 3–9, leaving a pronounced left-margin gutter that echoes classical Korean jangjeong binding space. Section index numeral sits flush left in the outer gutter, vertically centred beside the text block. A single hairline rule separates any subhead from body copy — no decorative bands, background panels, or header bar. Sequence folio mark appears bottom-right; the vermillion seal impression anchors bottom-left as colophon.
